data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resumption must be refused when token-budget exhaustion occurs inside a causally atomic reasoning step whose internal state was only partially flushed, because re-entering that step from the outside produces a different causal history than uninterrupted execution would have\u2014even though no committed event was modified or deleted.","counterconditions":[{"case":"All reasoning-envelope operations are individually idempotent and deterministic given the same input, making recomputation causally equivalent.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The step boundary is recoverable from the log itself via self-delimiting framing, making the truncation point an inter-step boundary by construction.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The causal fingerprint includes only committed events, not internal intermediate states, so recomputation is invisible to the fingerprint.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Some reasoning-envelope operations are causally atomic: they emit a single event that summarizes a multi-token internal computation. If exhaustion interrupts the internal computation before the summarizing event is emitted, the resumption protocol sees no event for that step. Restarting the step from scratch is physically append-only-safe (nothing was committed to delete), but logically it produces a different causal fingerprint because the recomputation may draw different random samples, encounter different cache states, or take a different internal path. The physical invariant is intact; the logical invariant is violated. Hence resumption is refused for atomic-step-internal truncation and permitted only at inter-step boundaries.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
